19.01.01.context: Checkout reserves three of five units.
19.01.01.concept: Unit tests isolate a rule; integration tests cross real boundaries; E2E tests traverse the user workflow.
19.01.01.exercise: Assert reserve(5,3) and outline a DB transaction test plus a browser checkout test. Label their boundaries.
19.01.01.negative: Overselling fails; passing the function test cannot prove concurrent DB safety.
19.01.01.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.02.context: An inventory refactor changes its private implementation.
19.01.02.concept: Assert observable behavior, not private method calls.
19.01.02.exercise: Assert reserve(3,3) and reserve(3,4); refactor internal code without changing behavior.
19.01.02.negative: An incorrect decrement on rejection must fail.
19.01.02.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.03.context: Two tests share a mutable cart object.
19.01.03.concept: Factories produce fresh objects with explicit defaults and overrides.
19.01.03.exercise: Create a factory returning stock 3 and quantity 1; mutate one instance and assert a second remains unchanged.
19.01.03.positive: Independent fixtures have identical initial state.
19.01.03.negative: Shared object mutation causes order-dependent tests.
19.01.03.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.04.context: An order expires at a deadline.
19.01.04.concept: Inject time rather than sleeping; define inclusive expiry semantics.
19.01.04.exercise: Write isExpired(expiresAt, now); check expiry=1000 at now=999,1000,1001.
19.01.04.positive: The order expires at 1000 and remains expired afterward.
19.01.04.negative: Using strict greater-than misses the deadline.
19.01.04.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.05.context: Inventory reservation invokes an email sender.
19.01.05.concept: Stub the external effect boundary; exercise the real reservation decision.
19.01.05.exercise: Inject a recorder as send function and invoke only after successful reserve.
19.01.05.negative: Rejected reservation records no send; provider delivery remains untested.
19.01.05.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.06.context: Warehouse stock must be conserved across many inputs.
19.01.06.concept: Properties are invariants over inputs; a finite sweep is deterministic, not exhaustive over all possible values.
19.01.06.exercise: Extend the lab finite property sweep to stock and quantity up to 50.
19.01.06.positive: Remaining stock plus accepted quantity equals original stock.
19.01.06.negative: Subtracting a rejected quantity breaks conservation.
19.01.06.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.07.concept: Coverage measures execution, not strength of assertions; mutation exposes weak checks.
19.01.07.exercise: In a disposable lab copy replace the rejection result with a success. Run the negative test.
19.01.07.positive: The mutation is caught by an assertion.
19.01.07.negative: A suite that merely executes the denial branch misses it.
19.01.07.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.01.08.context: A developer builds a reservation feature test-first.
19.01.08.concept: Red-green-refactor starts with meaningful failing behavior, then minimum correction and refactoring.
19.01.08.exercise: In a disposable copy make reserve return unchanged stock; run tests, repair it, add zero-stock coverage.
19.01.08.positive: Intended behavior assertions fail then pass.
19.01.08.negative: A syntax error is not a meaningful red test.
19.01.08.boundary: Pure inventory model; no real database or browser is tested.

19.02.01.context: A settings form shows loading and saved status.
19.02.01.concept: Vitest runs tests; Testing Library encourages testing from the user's perspective.
19.02.01.exercise: Run latestRequest; in an installed React fixture click Save with user-event and await the visible saved message.
19.02.01.negative: Rejected requests show accessible errors, not only mock invocations.
19.02.01.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.02.context: An icon-only Save button has a hidden text label.
19.02.02.concept: Accessible role and name describe control semantics rather than classes.
19.02.02.exercise: In a real DOM fixture query `getByRole('button', {name: 'Save'})`; change its CSS class and rerun.
19.02.02.negative: Removing the accessible name breaks the test.
19.02.02.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.03.context: Two search requests finish out of order.
19.02.03.concept: The newest request owns the current UI state; earlier results must be ignored.
19.02.03.exercise: Start A and B in latestRequest, resolve B then A; translate into a real React interaction test.
19.02.03.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.04.context: A frontend test needs a server error without production access.
19.02.04.concept: MSW intercepts at the network boundary so the app still uses its real client.
19.02.04.exercise: In an installed MSW fixture supply synthetic 200 and 503 handlers, reject unhandled requests, reset handlers per test.
19.02.04.negative: 503 produces the intended retry/error state; no external request.
19.02.04.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.05.context: A registration form rejects an invalid email.
19.02.05.concept: Client validation helps usability; the server remains authoritative.
19.02.05.exercise: In a real form test enter invalid email, submit, inspect its associated error, correct it and submit again.
19.02.05.negative: Invalid input exposes the error and makes no submit call.
19.02.05.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.06.context: A responsive card clips its text after a layout change.
19.02.06.concept: Visual baselines depend on viewport, fonts, data and browser; they require review.
19.02.06.exercise: Capture a fixed browser fixture at narrow and wide widths; deliberately clip its title and inspect the screenshot diff.
19.02.06.positive: Unchanged fixture matches the reviewed baseline.
19.02.06.negative: Clipping changes the snapshot; do not blindly accept updates.
19.02.06.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.07.context: A modal must work without a mouse.
19.02.07.concept: Keyboard order, visible focus and restoration are behavioral requirements; manual assistive technology review remains necessary.
19.02.07.exercise: Tab to the trigger, open with Enter, traverse controls, close with Escape, verify focus restoration in a real browser.
19.02.07.positive: The keyboard user can operate and dismiss the dialog.
19.02.07.negative: Trapped focus or a mouse-only close action fails.
19.02.07.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.02.08.context: A flaky test waits an arbitrary 500 ms.
19.02.08.concept: Await observable behavior instead of a fixed sleep; control response order deterministically.
19.02.08.exercise: Run latestRequest reversal case and replace a fixed browser wait with an awaited visible result.
19.02.08.positive: The expected result is stable across completion orders.
19.02.08.negative: Retries do not repair a stale-response defect.
19.02.08.boundary: Plain JavaScript UI state model; installed React/Vitest/Testing Library/MSW and real browsers require separate tests.

19.03.01.context: A Nest service depends on a repository provider.
19.03.01.concept: Testing modules construct dependency graphs; overrides replace a specific provider boundary.
19.03.01.exercise: In installed Nest build Test.createTestingModule with a feature module, override its repository, compile and resolve the service.
19.03.01.negative: Omitting the provider produces a resolution error.
19.03.01.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.02.context: A task service returns a minimal owner DTO.
19.03.02.concept: Assert authorization and public data shape rather than private persistence fields.
19.03.02.exercise: Call scopedRead for the owner and add a private field to the input row; assert exact response keys.
19.03.02.positive: Only id and title are returned.
19.03.02.negative: Foreign owner or private field leakage fails.
19.03.02.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.03.context: A protected API route is invoked over HTTP.
19.03.03.concept: Integration covers routing, middleware, serialization and auth, not just a function call.
19.03.03.exercise: Use an installed local API on an ephemeral loopback port; send anonymous, owner and foreign-tenant requests.
19.03.03.positive: Owner receives 200 and the documented DTO.
19.03.03.negative: Anonymous receives 401; foreign tenant receives the specified 404.
19.03.03.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.04.context: A DB test modifies rows before failing.
19.03.04.concept: Rollback isolates changes only on the same transaction and connection.
19.03.04.exercise: In a disposable PostgreSQL DB seed data, BEGIN, update then force failure, ROLLBACK and query via a fresh connection.
19.03.04.negative: Separately committed updates escape rollback and must be detected.
19.03.04.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.05.context: A migration adds a non-null field to existing rows.
19.03.05.concept: Migrations need representative old data, compatibility and explicit backfill.
19.03.05.exercise: Apply the previous schema in a disposable DB, seed a legacy row, apply expansion and backfill, then validate constraints.
19.03.05.positive: Legacy rows survive and new writes satisfy the schema.
19.03.05.negative: Unresolved nulls prevent enforcement; never test on production.
19.03.05.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.06.context: A multi-tenant service depends on database RLS.
19.03.06.concept: RLS must be tested with restricted non-owner/non-BYPASSRLS roles, not merely UI filters.
19.03.06.exercise: Use scopedRead as a contract, then run a P5 RLS qualification with real restricted role and transaction-local claims.
19.03.06.negative: Missing and foreign context cannot expose data.
19.03.06.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.07.context: A client depends on a stable task response.
19.03.07.concept: Contracts assert semantics; snapshots require review and should not accept private fields.
19.03.07.exercise: Assert exact scopedRead DTO; compare a real HTTP payload against a reviewed schema or snapshot.
19.03.07.negative: Removed keys or added secret fields fail.
19.03.07.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.03.08.context: A request must authenticate, authorize, query and serialize.
19.03.08.concept: Layered unit checks and real request tests verify different risks.
19.03.08.exercise: Use scopedRead acceptance targets to implement a Nest route against disposable DB; exercise real owner/anonymous/foreign requests.
19.03.08.positive: Authorized HTTP request returns the expected minimal DTO.
19.03.08.negative: Denied requests cannot reveal or modify rows.
19.03.08.boundary: Synthetic row/actor model; no Nest DI, network server, PostgreSQL or RLS execution.

19.04.01.context: An API must sustain a bounded workload.
19.04.01.concept: Scenarios specify executors and workload shape; predefine thresholds.
19.04.01.exercise: Design a small k6 constant-arrival-rate scenario against a disposable loopback service; compare samples with latencyReport.
19.04.01.positive: Latency and error thresholds are evaluated.
19.04.01.negative: Threshold violation fails; never target production.
19.04.01.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.02.context: Most requests are fast, but the tail is slow.
19.04.02.concept: Nearest-rank p95 is the sorted sample at ceil(.95*n)-1; averages can hide outliers.
19.04.02.exercise: Use 18 samples at 10ms and two at 1000ms; compare mean with p95.
19.04.02.negative: A mean-only gate can conceal a bad tail.
19.04.02.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.03.context: A query slows when a connection pool saturates.
19.04.03.concept: Distinguish pool waiting, query execution, locks and resource pressure.
19.04.03.exercise: In disposable DB benchmark a fixed query at two bounded concurrency levels; record p95 and errors, inspect EXPLAIN.
19.04.03.negative: Dropping failures or exhausting shared DB capacity invalidates the run.
19.04.03.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.04.context: Independent workers compete to claim one task.
19.04.04.concept: Concurrency tests need real overlapping attempts and invariant checks.
19.04.04.exercise: Review and run existing P5 multiprocess inbox tests; plan a separate real PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED test.
19.04.04.positive: Local model grants at most one competing claim.
19.04.04.negative: Double-claim fails; file lock evidence is not database proof.
19.04.04.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.05.context: A local dependency becomes unavailable temporarily.
19.04.05.concept: Chaos needs an isolated target, bounded fault, hypothesis and recovery criterion.
19.04.05.exercise: Inject a deterministic failure into a disposable handler; measure with latencyReport and restore the handler.
19.04.05.positive: Error rate returns to the target after recovery.
19.04.05.negative: Unbounded retries or zero samples fail the experiment.
19.04.05.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.06.context: A protected route accidentally exposes a secret field.
19.04.06.concept: Security regressions specify an abuse case and observable denial.
19.04.06.exercise: Extend scopedRead with a foreign tenant and private field; separately test the real HTTP boundary and dependency audit.
19.04.06.negative: Leaked fields or unauthorized records fail.
19.04.06.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.07.context: A test suite is divided into several shards.
19.04.07.concept: Aggregation verifies distinct expected shard identities and exact commit.
19.04.07.exercise: Use matrixGate for shard-1, shard-2, shard-3; omit a result.
19.04.07.positive: All expected shards must pass on one commit.
19.04.07.negative: Missing, duplicated or stale results fail.
19.04.07.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

19.04.08.context: A team defines a measurable API SLO.
19.04.08.concept: Specify the population, window, measurement method and targets before sampling.
19.04.08.exercise: Make 100 synthetic samples, one failure and p95 below 100ms; add two failures and re-evaluate.
19.04.08.positive: First set meets p95 100ms and error rate 1%.
19.04.08.negative: Changed set fails; this is not real production SLA proof.
19.04.08.boundary: Metrics model uses supplied samples; no real load generation, chaos or database benchmark.

20.01.01.context: A mutable image tag differs across machines.
20.01.01.concept: Images have immutable digest identity; containers are runtime instances with writable state.
20.01.01.exercise: Compare a synthetic digest and tag-only input to containerPolicy; inspect a real Docker image digest separately.
20.01.01.positive: Digest form meets the pinning policy.
20.01.01.negative: A mutable tag alone fails the model.
20.01.01.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.02.context: A final runtime image includes unnecessary compilers.
20.01.02.concept: Multi-stage builds separate build tooling from runtime; copy only required outputs.
20.01.02.exercise: Sketch builder and runtime stages; in disposable Docker build and inspect final layers and size.
20.01.02.positive: Runtime contains only required artifacts and dependencies.
20.01.02.negative: Copied credentials or unnecessary tooling fail review.
20.01.02.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.03.context: An API boots before the database is ready.
20.01.03.concept: Startup order is not readiness; health checks and bounded retries are separate.
20.01.03.exercise: Require a healthcheck in containerPolicy; in real Compose test a service_healthy dependency with a failed DB.
20.01.03.positive: API becomes usable only after DB is healthy.
20.01.03.negative: An unhealthy dependency cannot be treated as ready.
20.01.03.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.04.context: A DB container is recreated during development.
20.01.04.concept: Named volumes persist independently; bind mounts map host paths and permissions.
20.01.04.exercise: In disposable Docker seed a named volume, recreate without removing it and test a read-only config mount.
20.01.04.negative: Writes to read-only config fail; do not remove valuable volumes.
20.01.04.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.05.context: A DB port is accidentally exposed to the host.
20.01.05.concept: Network membership and published ports are distinct; expose only intended ingress.
20.01.05.exercise: Evaluate topologyPolicy; inspect real disposable Compose ports/network and test service-to-service connectivity.
20.01.05.negative: Public database port violates the design.
20.01.05.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.06.context: A container runs as root with broad write access.
20.01.06.concept: Prefer a non-root UID and restricted filesystem; deliberately provide needed writable paths.
20.01.06.exercise: Run containerPolicy with UID 1000 then UID 0; in Docker inspect identity and test writes.
20.01.06.negative: UID 0 or writable root is flagged.
20.01.06.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.07.context: A pinned base image has vulnerable packages.
20.01.07.concept: Pinning is reproducibility, not scanning. Review SBOM, advisory findings and provenance.
20.01.07.exercise: Run the pinning check; scan an actual local image separately and document digest and dispositions.
20.01.07.positive: Real findings have explicit review and blocking policy.
20.01.07.negative: Scanner outage or unknown digest cannot count as clean.
20.01.07.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.01.08.context: A developer needs an isolated API/database stack.
20.01.08.concept: A safe local stack combines reviewed images, non-root identity, health checks and network isolation.
20.01.08.exercise: Evaluate containerPolicy and topologyPolicy; create a disposable Compose exercise with synthetic data.
20.01.08.positive: Models pass and real health/isolation checks remain required.
20.01.08.negative: Privileged execution, exposed DB or Docker socket fails the policy.
20.01.08.boundary: Declarative policy model; no Docker engine, image build, scan or real network isolation executed.

20.02.01.context: A project checks two operating systems.
20.02.01.concept: Matrix jobs have distinct identities; aggregate all expected combinations.
20.02.01.exercise: Use matrixGate with linux-node24 and windows-node24; remove one result.
20.02.01.positive: Both platform results match the candidate commit.
20.02.01.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.02.context: Typecheck was skipped although build succeeded.
20.02.02.concept: Lint, typecheck, tests and build guard different failure domains.
20.02.02.exercise: Evaluate four required job identities with typecheck skipped.
20.02.02.positive: All four must be successful for one commit.
20.02.02.negative: Skipped or failed job blocks aggregation.
20.02.02.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.03.context: Cached dependencies come from a different lockfile.
20.02.03.concept: Cache keys include platform/runtime/lock digest; cache is not verification.
20.02.03.exercise: Compute SHA-256 for two lockfile fixtures; compare intended cache keys and require npm ci and tests on a hit.
20.02.03.negative: A cache hit cannot substitute acceptance.
20.02.03.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.04.context: A build log accidentally exposes a credential.
20.02.04.concept: Secrets require least-privilege access and isolation from untrusted code; masking alone is insufficient.
20.02.04.exercise: Design a fake secret and sanitized log fixture; review hypothetical PR job permissions without enabling Actions.
20.02.04.negative: Giving untrusted code a deployment secret fails.
20.02.04.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.05.context: A dependency update introduces a critical advisory.
20.02.05.concept: Scan genuine locks using current advisory data; exceptions need bounded review.
20.02.05.exercise: Inspect audit:dependencies; reason about a synthetic critical result and expired exception.
20.02.05.negative: Critical, expired or unavailable advisory evidence blocks qualification.
20.02.05.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.06.context: An artifact does not correspond to the tested commit.
20.02.06.concept: Bind an immutable digest and provenance to the tested commit; names alone prove nothing.
20.02.06.exercise: Use matrixGate with a stale commit; hash a local synthetic artifact and change one byte.
20.02.06.positive: Wrong commit fails and altered artifact hash changes.
20.02.06.negative: Edited artifact cannot inherit earlier evidence.
20.02.06.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.07.context: A branch accepts merges despite a missing check.
20.02.07.concept: Server-side branch protection enforces stable required check identities; local code is not server proof.
20.02.07.exercise: Model a missing required result; review hypothetical branch rules without changing the repo.
20.02.07.positive: Complete commit-bound result set meets the model.
20.02.07.negative: Missing evidence cannot authorize a merge.
20.02.07.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.02.08.context: A developer wants a local CI pipeline.
20.02.08.concept: Local commands and receipts support evidence without enabling cloud workflows.
20.02.08.exercise: Run matrixGate and inspect npm run qualify:academy:local -- --plan; design expected jobs.
20.02.08.positive: Each modeled result is tied to one commit.
20.02.08.negative: Missing or recursive jobs fail the relevant audit; no Actions run.
20.02.08.boundary: Synthetic CI evidence only; no hosted workflow, branch protection change or cryptographic provenance.

20.03.01.context: A build has no environment approval.
20.03.01.concept: Authorization is independent of successful code checks.
20.03.01.exercise: Call releaseDecision with approved=false then true, holding other evidence valid.
20.03.01.positive: All true conditions promote the candidate.
20.03.01.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.02.context: A migration renames a field used by old app instances.
20.03.02.concept: Expand-contract adds compatible structure, backfills and transitions readers before destructive cleanup.
20.03.02.exercise: Set compatible=false; in a disposable DB test old and new queries against expanded schema.
20.03.02.negative: Incompatibility holds release; destructive rollback may lose data.
20.03.02.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.03.context: A rolling deployment has old and new app instances.
20.03.03.concept: Versions need shared schema/API compatibility; readiness and draining control traffic.
20.03.03.exercise: Draw two-instance replacement sequence and model a healthy then unhealthy candidate.
20.03.03.negative: Unready candidate should not receive traffic; real balancing still untested.
20.03.03.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.04.context: A process listens but cannot reach its DB.
20.03.04.concept: Liveness, readiness and functional smoke answer different questions.
20.03.04.exercise: Set health=true and smoke=false; in a real local service test readiness plus synthetic user operation.
20.03.04.positive: Both readiness and functional smoke succeed before promotion.
20.03.04.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.05.context: A new version breaks checkout after release.
20.03.05.concept: Rollback selects a known compatible artifact, not a new arbitrary build.
20.03.05.exercise: Model v2 and previous v1 with failed smoke; write a rollback receipt naming the previous digest.
20.03.05.negative: Incompatible schema holds rollout; rollback safety still requires real verification.
20.03.05.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.06.context: A feature is exposed to a small cohort.
20.03.06.concept: Feature flags separate deployment from exposure; defaults and stable cohort identity matter.
20.03.06.exercise: Design deterministic assignment and default-off behavior; model incompatible flag contract as held.
20.03.06.positive: Same subject stays in the same cohort.
20.03.06.negative: Flag-service failure must not unexpectedly enable exposure.
20.03.06.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.07.context: A release elevates error rates off-hours.
20.03.07.concept: Incident-ready delivery defines ownership, abort threshold, evidence and recovery path.
20.03.07.exercise: Write a synthetic receipt containing artifact ID, threshold, reviewer, action; model failed health.
20.03.07.positive: Decision maps to a predefined abort condition.
20.03.07.negative: Missing owner or health evidence does not qualify release.
20.03.07.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.03.08.context: A learner rehearses deploy and rollback locally.
20.03.08.concept: Exercise hold, promotion and rollback without contacting live hosts.
20.03.08.exercise: Run 20.03 tests; simulate healthy candidate, failed smoke and missing approval.
20.03.08.positive: Model promotes, rolls back or holds as intended.
20.03.08.negative: Unapproved/incompatible candidate stays held; no real deployment.
20.03.08.boundary: Boolean release decision model, not deployment, migration, traffic switching or verified rollback.

20.04.01.context: A Linux service stores a secret and writable data.
20.04.01.concept: Ownership and permissions grant only necessary access; avoid broad chmod fixes.
20.04.01.exercise: In a disposable directory create a fake secret; compare owner-only with world-readable permissions.
20.04.01.positive: Only intended local account reads the file.
20.04.01.boundary: Synthetic topology policy; no OS/firewall/TLS/DNS/IaC or restore enforcement tested.

20.04.02.context: Public ingress forwards to a private app.
20.04.02.concept: Reverse proxy routes traffic and handles TLS; forwarded headers need a trusted boundary.
20.04.02.exercise: Use public TLS edge/private app model; in local Caddy route synthetic requests and inspect headers.
20.04.02.negative: Direct public app or missing TLS fails.
20.04.02.boundary: Synthetic topology policy; no OS/firewall/TLS/DNS/IaC or restore enforcement tested.

20.04.03.concept: Validity period, chain, hostname and renewal are separate from a configured TLS flag.
20.04.03.exercise: Inspect a local test certificate and plan renewal monitoring; model tls=false.
20.04.03.positive: Real client verifies a valid chain/name and the model requires TLS.
20.04.03.negative: Expired or wrong-host certificate fails real verification.
20.04.03.boundary: Synthetic topology policy; no OS/firewall/TLS/DNS/IaC or restore enforcement tested.

20.04.04.context: DNS points to an old origin after migration.
20.04.04.concept: TTL governs cache lifetime; origin routing and CDN caches are separate.
20.04.04.exercise: Draw two resolver caches with 300-second TTL and a record change; plan compatible origins during transition.
20.04.04.positive: The plan handles stale and fresh addresses.
20.04.04.negative: Assuming instant propagation invalidates the plan.
20.04.04.boundary: Synthetic topology policy; no OS/firewall/TLS/DNS/IaC or restore enforcement tested.

20.04.05.context: A small VPS hosts a proxy, app and DB.
20.04.05.concept: Minimize open services, use patched software, service accounts, backups and tested firewall.
20.04.05.exercise: Evaluate topologyPolicy and sketch a disposable VM; list intended ports and verify from authorized local network.
20.04.05.positive: Public edge separated from private data services.
20.04.05.negative: Public DB or unverified restore fails; no live host changes.
